independent_review.why_this_scope_is_high_risk: CHANGE TEAM and CRITICAL are fundamentally about MULTI-IMAGE execution. Almost every interesting obligation is a dynamic cross-image requirement that no conforming single-image program can observe, and that a processor is not required to diagnose. The dominant failure mode is a facet that looks testable but is unimplementable in both directions.

permission_restriction_split: Both sentences take the form 'It is permissible to branch to an END TEAM / END CRITICAL statement ONLY from within its construct'. Each therefore carries a permission and, through the word 'only', a paired restriction boundary. The reviewer confirmed the packet captures both halves, consistent with the precedent set in batch111.

findings.source_text: All active images of the new team shall execute the same CHANGE TEAM statement.
findings.defect: The same-statement and same-count violation was filed as a DIAGNOSTIC REJECTION - a negative with a control, expecting a processor to reject the invalid program. But the rule is a dynamic multi-image synchronization obligation on the PROGRAM, not a statically diagnosable constraint. Which CHANGE TEAM statement each active image executes is determined at run time and depends on which image runs which code path. A conforming processor is neither required to diagnose a violation nor generally able to, and there is no portable executable oracle either, since observing divergence would require exactly the timing, scheduling and interleaving evidence this project forbids. The facet was therefore unimplementable in BOTH directions.
findings.closure: S11.1.5.2-005's diagnostic obligation is now 'not-required'; the facet was recast from 'different-change-team-statement-rejected' to 'same-statement-count-violation-unimplementable-source-control'; and the plan text states explicitly that this is a dynamic multi-image program obligation with no required diagnostic and no portable executable oracle in this suite's single-image regime. The requirement itself remains registered and still states the p5 obligation - only the unsupportable plan was removed.

observability_sweep.rule_established: A facet may carry a DIAGNOSTIC expectation only if a conforming processor is actually required to reject the program, and may carry an EXECUTABLE oracle only if a conforming single-image program can portably observe the effect. A dynamic multi-image synchronization obligation satisfies neither.
observability_sweep.scope: After C11TR-001 the author was required to sweep the entire packet against that test and produce a table classifying every facet as implementable, unimplementable-context-dependent, or source-control only.
observability_sweep.reviewer_audit: The reviewer audited the table against the source rather than accepting it, checking rows including the S11.1.5.2-001 FORM TEAM, current-team and team-restoration rows, all four p5 rows, the p6, p7 and p8 synchronization and precedence rows, S11.1.6-001, the S11.1.6-002 failure and block-completion rows, and every S11.1.6-003 row.
observability_sweep.over_suppression_check: Specifically checked, because an unobservability claim that is too broad is itself a defect in this project and under-claiming is no better than over-claiming. The team-restoration rows and the CRITICAL segment classification were examined for local single-image observability. No over-suppression was found.
observability_sweep.vacuity_check: No facet could pass vacuously in a single-image run - which would be worse than having no facet at all.

explicit_limitations: This batch registers source accounting only. It is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it creates no test case.
All 85 facets in scope remain pending, and a substantial fraction are recorded as UNIMPLEMENTABLE in this suite's single-image observational regime rather than merely unwritten.

No timing, scheduling, interleaving, race or mutual-exclusion observation is admitted anywhere. CRITICAL provides mutual exclusion, but a conforming program cannot portably observe that another image was excluded.
Failed-image material is documentary, because there is no portable way to induce a failed image.
Registering CHANGE TEAM and CRITICAL source does not give this suite any multi-image testing capability; acquiring one would be a separate, substantial piece of work.
No compiler was invoked during authoring or review. The eight substring executions integrated in batch099 remain the latest actual observations.
